recipes.name: Southern Pimento Cheese
ingredients_raw: salt and black pepper to taste

steps.text: Place Cheddar cheese, cream cheese, mayonnaise, pimento, minced jalapeño, garlic powder, cayenne pepper, and onion powder in a large bowl.
Season to taste with salt and black pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Southern Pimento Cheese
raw_recipe.description: Pimento cheese is jazzed up with jalapeño and cayenne pepper for a creamy spreadable cheese that’s delicious on crackers, as a dip, or in sandwiches.

video.description: Pimento cheese is a true Southern staple, and our top-rated recipe will help you create a version that keeps friends and family coming back for more. Use this cheesy spread to spice up grilled cheese sandwiches, as a topping for crackers, or served alongside your favorite fried green tomatoes.

review.reviewBody: Hey ya'll! Thanks for all the great reviews--I am so flattered! Thanks, also, for not making the recipe completely different than written and then stating how you don't like it. I don't understand that. Thanks again. Don't forget to use EXTRA-SHARP cheddar cheese! **UPDATE 6/24/2011** Thanks to Yakaty for suggesting the addition of worchestershire and mustard. It makes this even better IMO! Thanks again to all for the reviews! PS If it ain't Duke's, it ain't mayo! ;)

This was without a doubt the best pimento cheese I've ever had! I omitted the jalapenos, and bumped up the cayenne a bit since I like my pimento cheese with a bit of a bite to it. Other than that, this recipe is flawless. Thank you so much for sharing!

If I could give this 10 stars, I would. This is phenomenal! After eating the store bought all my life, I knew there had to be something better than that . I found a guy at a farmer's market who sells it homemade but he was charging $8 for a tiny container. After much griping from the hubby about spending that much on pimento cheese every week, I finally decided to try it myself & I am so glad I did. This blows farmer's market guy out of the water. The 1 tiny change I made was that I just used a hand mixer to mix the cream cheese, Mayo & spices. I folded in the grated cheese, jalapeno, & pimentos so it would maintain a chunky texture.

First time trying this and I liked the concept. True to form, I increased the cayenne just a little for a longer finish, added a tad of dry mustard, and some worcestershire sauce in the spirit of Beer Cheese soup. This recipe didn't need it from my tasting but it fit my taste. Time to give it to the troops to try.

This is a favorite at our house. I always make my own pimento as well, since the jarred stuff is so expensive. Just broil or roast a red pepper until the skin is black, stick in a plastic bag to cool, then peel off the skin and clean out the seeds. Fresh pimento!

Jalapeno is optional although it is good to make a double batch of this and add Jalapeno to the second batch. Make a grilled cheese from the Jalapeno batch using raisin bread, top burgers with it or add it to grits! There are countless ways to use Pimento cheese. And for heavens sake don't use Miracle Whip! The BEST mayo for pimento cheese is Duke's!! Hope you enjoy is as much as we do.

I added 1/4 teaspoon of garlic salt in the mixture. Whipped with a hand mixer the cream cheese, seasonings and dukes mayo for a creamer texture before folding in the jalapeño, cheese and pimentos. Also used Vermont extra sharp and yellow sharp cheddar. Delicious! Will make again.

Reading others reviews - it's funny how different we are in our tastes! I loved the recipe as is but I always try to make things a bit lighter and different. I cut the cream cheese and mayo in half and bumped up the garlic powder, onion powder and cayenne a bit because I liked the added heat and flavors. I also added a 1/3 cup of finely diced red bell pepper for texture . Great recipe!

All ingredients at room temp including bout half the cheese (very finely grated) blend til very creamy & smooth - fold in COLD coarsely grated remainder of cheese so it can be seen in the final mix and provide a tiny bit of texture.

I absolutely love this recipe. It is so easy. I made it the night before for a Christmas potluck, but added some diced green onion inside the dip and on top for garnish. I also added 2 TSP of Dan-O’s seasoning instead of the cayenne because my co-workers can’t handle spice, and subbed out the jalapeño for a finely diced poblano pepper to ensure it still had that nice pepper flavor without the heat level of a jalapeño. Topped with paprika. Was absolutely delicious. I served with sliced cucumber, seedless sweet mini peppers, cherry tomatoes, and some multigrain seed crackers. A tip: hand-grate the cheese!

I used pickled jalapenos instead of raw. A milder flavor but effective. For a creamier spread add a little boiling water to the recipe as you combine - not too much or it will become pimento cheese soup. ( I got this last tip from the Duke's sandwich shop in Greenville, SC, the home of Duke's mayo and the only mayo to use for Pimento Cheese.)
Always a hit! Absolutely delicious. As recommended by another I add dry mustard and Worcestershire sauce. I use a hand mixer to blend everything before adding the pimento.
Very easy. I didn’t change a thing. Love the “bite” at the end!

Made the recipe as written and loved it! Added a second jalapeño and loved it more. I keep it in a covered crock in the fridge for a quick and delicious snack (especially on Ritz crackers). I think it's the same recipe my mom used in the 1970s. It really takes me back. Thanks for posting!
I didn’t have enough X-sharp to shred, so I tweaked by using replacing 1c XS cheddar w/ 1/2c jack and 1/2c medium cheddar. Everyone loved it. BTW, this is best w/shreds directly from the block.
I used to spend a small fortune to buy a pimento cheese spread made in the south. With this recipe I will be happily making my own. Much better flavor than any store bought!!!

It’s a great recipe I use it all the time. The family loves it. I use 1/8 tsp of cayenne and 3 dashes of Louisiana brand hot sauce. Plus I added another cup of grated ES cheddar grated on the smaller holes of the box grater. I believe that makes it creamier.
Great recipe just added tablespoon of minced onion Vidalia. great for stuffing peppers or toasted on a baguette..

From: Texas G-mom I wanted to make this one day and I didn’t have any jalapeños, but I did have some spicy jalapeño cream cheese spread, so I use that in the place of the cream cheese and it turned out really good. I think maybe even better than when I have made it with fresh jalapeños in the past.

I am a creme cheese fanatic yet somehow I never thought of adding this to my Pimento Cheese! Adding the creme cheese is definitely the kicker. I made it for my husband who had never had it!(He's Dutch) He couldn't believe that it took 65 years for him to have this heavenly spread. I also made a pasta salad with it using elbow macaroni and I made an omelette with it. Double the pleasure!
